cells.place: On the top of the doorway in the same wall,
cells.remarks: Gift of a village on the bank of the Musi (river) by the mahā-mandaleśvara Vishṇuvardhana (Bhīma)rāja-Sīthyadēva-Mahārāja who was a worshipper of the god Bhīmēśvara of Daksha-rāṇa and was a worshipper of the god of Vengi. Furnishes the king's genealogy and records that the king's sister was Gōnkama-mahādēvī, daughter of Mahārāja Bēta, second son of Natavādi Buddha, built and consecrated the temple of the Mūlabhīmēśvara near that of Tripurāntaka. She granted some 26 gōts for a lamp. The village called Tirtalu and also gave 26 gōts for a lamp.

cells.place: On another slab set up in the same place.
cells.remarks: The north, east and south faces of the pillar, respectively, record (1) that Kōṭayya, the wife of Gōpī-nātha-ayya, had the temple of Vēdēśvara repaired; (2) that Haḍapada, the son of Kāmalāvara after her own name; (3) that Haḍapālam, the daughter of king Alluḍi, lord of the town of Munata, founded the shrine of Haḍapālasvara after her own name; (4) that the Pallava king Khāṇḍa-rāya of the solar race established the shrine called Pallavēśvara and the shrine of Vīrēśvara; (5) that the king of the solar race built the three shrines. The same Sanskrit verses are repeated on two other pillars in Nōgaṭ and Grantas characters. Mentions two Śaiva teachers.

cells.remarks: Records that Peda-Sūrama-Nāyaningāru of the Jōpalli family rebuilt the Nāganātha (or Nāgēśvara) temple of stone, dug a tank near it and granted land to the temple. cells.remarks: Gift of the village of Narava to Nrsimha of Simhadri by the Padmanayaka Surappa-Asvarayanigaru. cells.location: Namakkal
cells.place: On the north, west and south walls of the deserted temple on the hill
cells.remarks: The hill is called Tīravairakkal and the inscription records a grant of land by the resident of Eḍai-nāḍu to the temple here called Arulanāyinar alias Ediri[li]ppurumal. Mentions Lakshmanā-an-an son of the Gajapatidēva Tippa-rasa-Udaya. A Tamil copy of No. 6 is found on the same wall. Mentions the following drudas: Nayapara, Prakritipriya Naravā- [dhana], Utpalakarpaka, Udāradhīta, and refers to the Atiyēn-dra-Vishnugha and the Atiyēnavaya.

cells.place: On the right and left door-posts of the entrance into the same mandapa.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the door post (?) by the mahāmaṇḍaleśvara, Bhramadeva-Chōḷa-Mahārāja, grandson of Bhōgādēvī and Bhramadēva. The chief calls himself the worshipper of the divine and glorious lotus-feet of the (god) Bhōgēśvaradēva of Pāmidi, Rōḍḍa-nāḍu, and of Ādityabhaṭṭāraka of the same place, belonging to the Chālukya-Vārāṇasi, the lord of Ayōdhyā, lord of the town of Ayōdhyā, worshipper of the feet of Allāḷanātha, [Pū]rṇṇā-rāja-Pemmayadēva-Mahārāja. The hero had gone on an expedition to the Mārajavāḍi country and died at Dhārāśīrtha.

cells.place: On the rock called Minikimāñi near Muṇiki.
cells.remarks: The Sanskrit portion mentions the Gaṅga family and Koṅkuṇivarman. The introduction belongs to Kulōttuṅga I, whose name is not mentioned. But the name Rājakēsarivarman and the title Chakravarttin occur at the end the introduction. The date here noted is in accordance with the date of the construction of a channel to the tank at Uppanēlli in Maḍukūru-nāḍu in Vaḍa-Pulinuḍu, a sub-division of Porumbāṇapāḍi in Nigarili-Chōḷa-maṇḍalam. The channel was improved by the son of the chief who built it.

cells.remarks: Mathilated at the beginning. Stones out of order. The 9th year (of the king?) is referred to on one of the stones. Seems to record a gift of lamps. Refers to the seizure of Vikrama-Śōla Isuvara-muḍaiyār. Refers to an earlier inscription of Kulōttunga-chōladēva grant of the village of Madarānikallur alias Arin- davan-Sattamaṅgalam under the name Vikramasōla- nallur. Mentions the revenue settlement made in the 38th year of (Kulōttunga I.) and the revenue survey.
